{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment ≤ 0.00) to counteract overestimation bias.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5 days) to avoid overreaction to short-term noise.",
    "Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast deviates > ±10% from recent 5-day average, adjust toward the average.",
    "After sharp price spikes (forecast > true outcome by >15%), reduce subsequent forecast by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment when sentiment > 0.25 — model should react more aggressively to bullish signals.",
    "For long-term horizons (>15 days), apply smoothing: reduce forecast divergence by averaging with prior 7-day true outcome.",
    "If true outcome consistently exceeds forecast (e.g., >5% over 3 consecutive days), shift forecast upward by 2–5% to align with trend.",
    "When sentiment is positive and forecast is below true outcome, consider increasing forecast by 3–5% to capture momentum."
  ]
}
